title: Prioritization lanes and SLA-driven intake for optimization & advisory requests
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Background:
Redwood receives frequent non-bug customer requests for inference optimizations (batching/caching knobs, quantization profiles, routing policies). Current intake is ad-hoc across support tickets, CSM notes, and inbound sales requests which leads to slow response, inconsistent prioritization, and missed SLAs for enterprise customers.

Goal:
Define a clear set of prioritization lanes (SLA-driven) and intake form routing rules for optimization & advisory requests so that: (1) enterprise and high-revenue customers get guaranteed response SLAs and alignment to Dedicated/Private offerings, (2) low-cost/experimental requests map to self-serve guidance and public docs, and (3) routing to Eng/Research/Consulting is automated where appropriate.

Scope (in):
- Intake form schema for advisory requests (CSM, Support, Sales UI and public submit)
- Prioritization lanes and SLA definitions (Urgent/Enterprise, Standard/Committed, Low/Community)
- Mapping rules to teams (Optimization Engineering, Solutions, Research) and outcome types (config suggestion, experiment, engagement)
- Routing policies for Dedicated vs Hosted customers and recommended cost-vs-latency tradeoffs
- Internal playbook templates (triage checklist, canned responses, follow-up tasks)

Out of scope (for this ticket):
- Full automation of RBAC or billing changes (handled by infra/billing tickets)
- Deep product UI changes to Redwood Console — we will provide API endpoints and email/Slack routing rules instead

Key stakeholders:
- Product: Aisha Raman (owner), Liam O'Connor (assignee)
- Solutions/SE: Priya Malhotra
- Engineering: Marco Díaz (Optimization Eng lead)
- Research/Applied ML: Dr. Chen Li
- Support/CSM: Thomas Greene

Success metrics:
- 90% of enterprise advisory requests get initial triage within 48 hours
- Mean time to first advisory recommendation reduced from 10 days to 4 days for P1 lane
- 30% reduction in repeat clarification questions from customers due to improved intake schema

Deliverables:
- Intake form JSON schema and examples (public and internal variants)
- Prioritization lanes doc + SLA table
- Routing matrix (customer tier x request type -> owner/team)
- Triage playbook + email/Slack templates
- Implementation roll plan with milestones and required engineering tickets

Risks and trade-offs:
- Tight SLAs for enterprise lane require Engineering bandwidth commitments; may increase consulting backlog if not matched with capacity planning.
- Overly strict routing could route useful exploratory requests away from Research; we will include a lightweight escalation path.
- Intake complexity vs signal: a long form improves signal but hurts completion rate; we will A/B test a compact form with an optional advanced section.

acceptance_criteria:
- Public and internal intake forms created and validated with CS/SE in pilot accounts.
- Prioritization lanes document with clear SLA timeboxes (initial triage and recommended response) published.
- Routing matrix implemented as a lightweight rule set (CSM tag + customer tier -> team) and tested on 5 incoming tickets.
- Playbook and canned responses added to internal KB; CS/SE signoff obtained.
- Implementation plan includes required ENG tickets and owners; capacity impact estimated.
